introducedVocabulary.english: still; yet in a negative sentence

title: Change plural olla statements into negatives
summary: Change olemme, olette, or ovat into emme ole, ette ole, or eivät ole while keeping the subject and context.
objectives: Change olemme, olette, or ovat into emme ole, ette ole, or eivät ole while keeping the subject and context.
Apply the pattern using the supporting forms shown.

sections.title: Replace the affirmative verb
paragraphs: Change olemme, olette, or ovat into emme ole, ette ole, or eivät ole while keeping the subject and context.
The negative verb carries person agreement. Put the fixed form ole after it.

sections.title: Change the polarity only
paragraphs: Read the source and target meanings. Keep the subject and supplied context unchanged.
Choose the negative verb from the original subject, then add ole.
Vielä can mean “still” in an affirmative statement and “yet” in a negative one. He eivät ole täällä vielä means “They are not here yet”; keep vielä while choosing the negative verb.

examples.finnish: Me olemme täällä. → Me emme ole täällä.
examples.english: We are here. → We are not here.

examples.finnish: Te olette paikalla. → Te ette ole paikalla.
examples.english: You are present. → You are not present.

examples.finnish: He ovat kotona. → He eivät ole kotona.
examples.english: They are at home. → They are not at home.

commonMistakes: Do not change the subject or the supplied context.
Keep ole after the person-marked negative verb.

practiceExercises.prompt: Optional practice: Notice who the sentence is about. Change Me olemme kotona. “We are at home.” → ____ “We are not at home.” Keep the subject and context unchanged.
practiceExercises.explanation: Me changes from olemme to emme ole. The negative verb carries the person ending.

Correct. Me changes from olemme to emme ole. The negative verb carries the person ending.
“Te ette ole kotona.” does not fit this subject or construction. Me changes from olemme to emme ole. The negative verb carries the person ending.
“Me ei olemme kotona.” does not fit this subject or construction. Me changes from olemme to emme ole. The negative verb carries the person ending.
